rows.leftIndex:
Aokiji
One of the Marines' three Admirals, user of the Ice-Ice Fruit.
Has many wide-area Ice damage skills  that also Freeze, greatly limiting enemies' Speed.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Monday morning, Aokiji appears in the desert with his subordinates.
rows.rightIndex:
Ace
Son of Roger.
User of the Flame-Flame Fruit, skilled at wide-area Fire attacks.
The traits of his Logia fruit give Ace extra resistance to elemental and group damage.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Monday evening, Ace appears in Syrup Village.

rows.leftIndex:
Garp
The legendary hero.
A Marine hero with an illustrious record, fighting with a balance of offense and defense.
Years of battle experience give Garp high resistance to physical damage.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Tuesday morning, Garp appears in the desert with his subordinates, fearlessly taking on all challengers in the name of justice.
rows.rightIndex:
Whitebeard
The strongest man in the world.
A Tremor Human who ate the Tremor-Tremor Fruit, one of the legendary Four Emperors.
Whitebeard has the power to destroy the world and high resistance to physical damage.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Tuesday evening, Whitebeard appears in Syrup Village, crushing every enemy who dares challenge him.

rows.leftIndex:
Blackbeard
The legendary hero.
User of the Dark-Dark Fruit, one of the legendary Four Emperors.
The Dark-Dark Fruit gives Blackbeard high resistance to physical damage.
Blackbeard's special constitution makes him feel twice the pain of a normal person, so the first physical attack he takes each turn deals more damage
When the Wanted Boss opens on Wednesday morning, Blackbeard appears outside Alubarna. Challengers will feel the terrifying power of the "Man of Ultimate Evil" firsthand
rows.rightIndex:
Aokiji
One of the Marines' three Admirals, user of the Ice-Ice Fruit.
Has many wide-area Ice damage skills  that also Freeze, greatly limiting enemies' Speed.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Wednesday evening, Aokiji appears in the town of Cocoyasi Village.
Players who dare challenge him will face a powerful counterattack from Aokiji and his subordinates.

rows.leftIndex:
Crocodile
The "King of the Desert", user of the Sand-Sand Fruit.
Can raise wide-area sandstorms that deal Wind damage.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Thursday morning, Crocodile appears outside Alubarna.
rows.rightIndex:
Enel
"God", user of the Rumble-Rumble Fruit.
He beats the Magatama Drums to channel powerful lightning in wide-area attacks, with a chance to Paralyze.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Thursday evening, Enel appears in Shandora

rows.leftIndex:
Bartholomew Kuma
User of the Paw Pad Fruit and former member of the Seven Warlords of the Sea.
With his fruit's power he forms paw-shaped air bullets that, once compressed and released, unleash terrifying shockwaves.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Friday morning, Kuma appears outside Alubarna.
rows.rightIndex:
Franky
The Straw Hats' shipwright, a cyborg.
His whole body has been modified, letting him use all kinds of ranged/melee attacks from different body parts to suit any battle situation.
When the Wanted Boss opens on Friday evening, Franky appears in the Little Garden wilds

rows.leftIndex:
Shanks
Nicknamed Red-Haired, one of the legendary Four Emperors.
A top swordsman with full control of Haki, even Conqueror's Haki.
Shanks races enemies to strike first; if Shanks is faster, he deals more damage
When the Wanted Boss opens on Saturday morning, Shanks appears in the town of Cocoyasi Village
rows.rightIndex:
Rayleigh
Known as the Dark King, former first mate of the Roger Pirates.
Master of all three types of Haki.
Rayleigh's combat skills raise his own Evasion
When the Wanted Boss opens on Saturday evening, Rayleigh appears in the Little Garden wilds

rows.leftIndex:
Ivankov
Queen of the Kamabakka Kingdom, the "Miracle Person".
User of the Hormone-Hormone Fruit with powerful support abilities.
Ivankov reduces the direct damage he takes, but takes more reflected damage
When the Wanted Boss opens on Sunday morning, Ivankov appears in the town of Cocoyasi Village
rows.rightIndex:
Marco
Commander of the Whitebeard Pirates' 1st Division, user of the rare Mythical Zoan "Bird-Bird Fruit, Model: Phoenix".
Has incredible regeneration and assault abilities.
Marco's strong surprise attacks deal more damage to players with Shields
When the Wanted Boss opens on Sunday evening, Marco appears in the Little Garden wilds

rows.buffTxt: When gaining [Dragon Scale], also gain [Scales]. At battle start, immediately gain 1 stack of [Scales]
[Scales] gained also trigger when Tenacity is 0, restoring 30% Tenacity
Ultimates in every state can stack [Scales]
Soul Jade cost -2. After using a Finisher or Ultimate for the first time, gain 10 Soul Jade.
When attacked, gain 8% Tenacity Defense for each 1 Soul Jade remaining.

After acting, gain 1 [Fury] energy for each 1 Soul Jade remaining. After using a [Finisher or Ultimate] in [Dragon-Human] state, if there is 20 [Fury] energy, consume it to follow up with [Drunken Dragon Bagua: Drunken Rage]. If [Drunken Dragon Bagua: Drunken Rage] hits a target whose Tenacity is 0, the target is instantly defeated. [Drunken Dragon Bagua: Drunken Rage] uses a 10-cost Finisher multiplier

In [Dragon-Human] state, attacking builds [Thunder]. When gaining [Thunder], own Speed +15% and Tenacity Break efficiency +10%; when gaining [Thunder], Crit Damage +30%. Stacks up to 3 times, lasts 3 turns.
When attacking in [Dragon-Human] state, each stack of [Thunder] raises own Crit Damage by 50% of current Crit Damage, up to 3 times

In [Dragon-Human] state, when attacking a target: with 1 [Thunder], a hit adds 1 extra Tenacity Damage hit equal to 50% of total Tenacity Attack; with 2 [Thunder], attacks nullify the target's skill-damage-limiting effects and Invincibility; with 3 [Thunder], gain Sure Hit and Accuracy +100% (new servers: Accuracy only). When acting in Dragon-Human state with 3 [Thunder], gain the skill [Thunder Bagua] (0 CD, 0 cost; consumes all [Thunder] when used; 10-cost Finisher multiplier).

When gaining [Dragon Scale], also gain [Scales]. Each time [Scales] has been gained, own All Damage Bonus +200%, Final Damage Bonus +100%, Attack Bonus +300% and Accuracy +100%, stacking up to 3 times.
While [Scales] are present, attacks can't be interrupted. On the first action, removes all debuffs and control effects
In the first 3 turns, after each action each [Scales] restores 10% Tenacity.
Each action raises Tenacity Attack by 10%, stacking up to 3 times, lasts 3 turns.
In [Dragon] state, each attack builds [Fire Dragon Energy]. Each stack of [Fire Dragon Energy] adds 10% Tenacity Damage in [Dragon] state.

In [Dragon] state, with 5 stacks of [Fire Dragon Energy], after using an Ultimate, consume 5 stacks to follow up with [Flame Dragon Torch]. [Flame Dragon Torch] uses a 10-cost Finisher multiplier and adds 5 bouncing hits of extra Tenacity Damage at 120% of total Tenacity Attack, Stunning targets for 1 action, up to 2 targets.
In [Human] state, skill attacks restore Tenacity, 5% each time
In [Dragon-Human] state, Tenacity Crit +30%, Tenacity Crit Damage +50%
In [Dragon] state, every attack that hits spreads 1 extra Tenacity Damage hit equal to 50% of own total Tenacity Attack to all enemies

At battle start, uses a special skill to devour all allied units. For each 1 unit devoured, gain 100% Attack, 150% Crit Damage, Tenacity Attack equal to 10% of the target's initial Attack and Tenacity equal to 65% of its max HP, up to 4 stacks. Finishers and Ultimates can also stack [Fire Dragon Energy]. If Rage is 100 after acting, immediately uses [Flame Dragon Torch], whose skill multiplier is then increased by 100%

Gain 1 extra action for every 2 units devoured, up to 2. After each action, Speed is reduced by 10% of current Speed; resets at the start of the turn. When this talent's extra actions trigger, Speed is reduced by 10% of current Speed

Gain 1 stack of [Dragon Might] after each action. When using an Ultimate with 5 stacks of [Dragon Might], consume them all to [Intimidate] the target for 1 action. When an [Intimidated] target attacks Kaido, 50% of its Tenacity Damage is lost.

Gain Tenacity equal to 200% of initial HP and Tenacity Defense equal to 50% of initial Defense. While Tenacity remains, HP can't drop below 50%. Each time an attack is dodged, Accuracy +100%, stacking up to 6 times.
Gain Tenacity Break equal to 50% of initial Attack, Tenacity Crit equal to initial Crit, and 150% Tenacity Crit Damage. Any initial Crit Damage above 150% is converted to Crit Damage at 60%

At battle start, Speed, Accuracy and HP +170%. After the first turn starts, Speed rises by 50% of current Speed, 3 times in a row. After each of Kaido's actions, Attack permanently rises by 35% of current Attack, Crit Damage permanently +80% and Final Damage Bonus permanently +30%, stacking up to 12 times and up to 3 times per turn.
Attacks apply "Vulnerable". Targets with "Vulnerable" take 15% more Tenacity Damage, stacking up to 3 times.
Before each action, each stack of "Vulnerable" deals extra Tenacity Damage equal to 30% of the source's total Tenacity Attack.
When attacking a target with 3 stacks of "Vulnerable", "Vulnerable" immediately settles 1 extra Tenacity Damage hit.

rows.name: Scholar Robe
rows.intro: Clothes worn by scholars while studying on the Sky Island. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: All elemental resistances +300 in battle.\nEffect 2: Elemental damage taken -25%.

rows.name: Withering Battle Coat
rows.intro: A coat a tribal chief always wore while ruling the tribe. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Team Attack and Defense +2%, stacking up to 5 times.\nEffect 2: When a teammate falls, immediately restore 10% HP.

rows.name: Knight Robe
rows.intro: Fine clothes a knight loves to wear in daily life. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Armor Break trigger chance +30%.\nEffect 2: When the character stands in the front row of the formation, damage reduction +15%.

rows.name: Slasher Uniform

rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Execute effect +15%.\nEffect 2: Defeating an enemy grants 2 Soul Jade and 10 Rage.

rows.name: Redbone Tunic

rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: After entering battle, Attack and Crit Rate +5%.\nEffect 2: Below 65% HP, immune to Stun and damage +10%.

rows.name: Warrior Armor
rows.intro: Clothes a warrior wore while roaming the world. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: After entering battle, Attack and HP +5%.\nEffect 2: On the first turn, Attack, Defense and Crit Rate +10%.

rows.name: Starlight Outfit
rows.intro: A battle outfit formed from gathered starlight. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Healing dealt +20%.\nEffect 2: Own HP +10%, and healing received +15%.

rows.name: Dragon Scale Shining Armor
rows.intro: A battle robe decorated with the scales of a giant dragon after defeating it. As armor, it adds some Defense and HP.
rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Damage of all-target skills +10%.\nEffect 2: Damage of each line skill +15%.

rows.name: Sentinel Uniform

rows.name: Resolve Retainer's Outfit

rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: After entering battle, Attack and Defense +5%.\nEffect 2: Crit Rate +10%; Speed +15% when worn by a female character.

rows.suitIntro: Effect 1: Crit Rate +5%, Crit Damage +15%.\nEffect 2: When your Soul Jade skills crit, there's a high chance to refund the Soul Jade spent on that skill.

rows.leftIndex:
Every 1000 servers form a region, and each region has 10 groups.
[Event Schedule]
Sign-up: Monday, Friday.
Sea Battle: Tuesday, Saturday evening 19:30-22:02.
[Basic Rules]
(1) A guild must reach Lv2 and have at least 30 members to sign up for Sea Battle.
(2) Each Guild Sea Battle season lasts 8 weeks. Points reset on the Monday of a new season.
(3) The system automatically matches guilds with similar points for simultaneous sea battles. Winning earns points; losing costs points.
rows.rightIndex:
(4) Destroying all enemy warships or capturing the enemy base counts as a victory.
(5) Each Sea Battle lasts 30 minutes. If there's no winner after 30 minutes, the side holding more outposts wins; if both hold the same number, it's a draw.
(6) In a draw, both sides count as losers.
(7) After each Sea Battle, the guild and its members receive rewards.
(8) Participating guilds automatically gain 300 Guild EXP per battle, win or lose.
(9) Auto-Play is allowed in Sea Battle, but players on Auto-Play earn less Guild Contribution.

rows.leftIndex:
[Reward Rules]
Guild rewards:
(1) The winning guild gets Guild Medals, Sea Battle Points, Crystals and Guild EXP.
(2) The losing side gets Guild Medals, Guild EXP and Crystals.
(3) Base points: +50 for a win, -50 for a loss.
(4) Bonus points: after a win, the guild gets 1 extra point for every 6 surviving fleets.
Personal rewards: after a Sea Battle, players get Guild Contribution and Sea Battle Coins; members who don't use Auto-Play get more Contribution.
(The extra Contribution above doesn't stack and can only be earned once per Sea Battle)
rows.rightIndex: Season rewards: the top 50 guilds get limited-time title rewards. Check the Sea Battle Rankings screen for details.

rows.leftIndex:
Sea Battle Tech Optimization
After the Sea Battle tech optimization, guild resources spent upgrading outposts are refunded
Outpost upgrades are removed for all outposts; once unlocked, an outpost has the strength of a max-level outpost
Upgrade the Command Center to get new outposts; each Command Center level unlocks new outposts.
Guild Leaders and Vice Leaders spend guild resources to build outposts, which go into storage for use in Sea Battle.
During outpost deployment, only built outposts can be deployed, so leaders, please build outposts in advance just in case.
rows.rightIndex: New Outposts (1)\nRally Outpost: once built, it can rally a number of offline Auto-Play allies. When the rally is complete, tapping any other outpost shows a "Charge" button; tap it to send all rallied Auto-Play allies to the target outpost.\nTsunami Cannon Outpost: can attack all enemy warships on the same route.

rows.leftIndex: New Outposts (2)\nTailwind Outpost: once built, all routes adjacent to the outpost become tailwind routes, doubling the movement speed of all our warships on them\nHeadwind Outpost: once built, all routes adjacent to the outpost become headwind routes, halving the movement speed of all enemy warships on them
rows.rightIndex: New Outposts (3)\nDock Outpost: periodically builds a time-limited warship that heads for the enemy headquarters and attacks any enemies it meets.\nAdvanced Dock Outpost: periodically builds a stronger time-limited warship that heads for the enemy headquarters and attacks any enemies it meets.

rows.leftIndex: (1) For Guild War, the Guild Leader or a Vice Leader must sign up the guild on sign-up day; after that, guild members can sign up individually.\n(2) Only after signing up individually can you join the Sea Battle lineup, otherwise you won't be able to take part in the Sea Battle!\n(3) To sign up individually, set your battle lineup first. You can set it once the Dock is unlocked.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_2_2;UnionCommandHelp_2_3

rows.leftIndex:
(1) A guild that meets the Sea Battle requirements can declare war.
(2) Only the Guild Leader or a Vice Leader can declare war.
(3) A guild can declare war and be declared on once every Wednesday.
(4) Winning a declared war earns Sea Battle Medals, Guild Crystals, guild points and personal Contribution.
(5) If no one declares war on your guild, the next day's rewards for that round are given as a win.
(6) While a declaration is active, you can't kick members, disband the guild and so on, and members can't leave the guild.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_10_2

rows.leftIndex:
(1) After the guild signs up, the matchups are announced after 0:00 the next day, and the Guild Leader or Vice Leaders can make Sea Battle preparations on the Sea Battle Deployment screen!
(2) The Guild Leader and Vice Leaders must go to Sea Battle Deployment in the Command Center to plan the coming battle. Deployment has two stages: personnel deployment and outpost deployment. When deploying personnel, Vice Leaders can only use Quick Deploy, which deploys signed-up members from highest to lowest Power. Vice Leaders can't deploy outposts.
(3) Members set for battle in personnel deployment take part in the Sea Battle. Members not deployed won't fight, but can still enter the battlefield to spectate and get the same Sea Battle rewards as deployed members.
(4) In outpost deployment you can choose which outpost techs to bring; outpost techs can upgrade normal outposts during battle!
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_3_2;UnionCommandHelp_3_3

rows.leftIndex:
(1) In Battle Settings you can adjust the crew and warships you use in Sea Battle.
(2) Each member can set two fleets. The 1st Fleet sails first in Sea Battle, and the 2nd Fleet sails after the 1st Fleet is defeated.
(3) In each Sea Battle round, once all your fleets are defeated, you get one reorganization, after which your fleets can sail again.
(4) After reorganization, if only one fleet was set, only one fleet can sail again.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_4_2;UnionCommandHelp_4_3

rows.leftIndex: (1) Once the Sea Battle opens, members can enter! Deployed members can fight, and other members can spectate.\n(2) Members can enter via the "Enter Sea Battle" button in the Command Center or on the main screen.\n(3) Deployed captains can control their warships, and captains not deployed can still spectate!
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_4_2;UnionCommandHelp_5_2

rows.leftIndex:
(1) The battlefield is split into the Blue side and the Red side, so captains, know your color!
(2) The base is the most important thing on the battlefield. If the enemy captures it, you lose immediately!
(3) Each route can only hold so many warships, so plan your routes well.
(4) Captured outposts must be garrisoned; an ungarrisoned outpost turns neutral.
(5) Normal outposts can be upgraded into advanced functional outposts. The Guild Leader must set techs in Sea Battle Deployment before the battle.
(6) Each upgrade tech brought can only be used 1 time, and only normal outposts can be upgraded.
(7) The Guild Leader or a Vice Leader can upgrade outposts. The upgrader must stay garrisoned in the outpost until the upgrade finishes; leaving midway makes it fail.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_6_2;UnionCommandHelp_6_3

rows.leftIndex:
(1) During Sea Battle you can still chat with friends outside or in World chat. Tap the battle status at the bottom left to open the chat box!
(2) Battle Replay lets you view the battles fought in this Sea Battle, and you can enter the battle scene to watch them.
(3) If you're still unsure about outposts and routes, the Help button may help.
(4) The Auto-Play button makes your warships sail automatically, but we don't recommend it, since it may reduce the Guild Contribution you earn in the end.
(5) The button at the bottom right of the screen quickly finds your own warships.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_7_2

rows.leftIndex:
(1) You can open the Settings screen during Sea Battle to adjust sound settings.
(2) Only Free Talk, Hide UI and Play Sea Battle Voice differ from the regular settings.
(3) Free Talk only works for the Guild Leader and Vice Leaders; other members can't give voice commands in Sea Battle.
(4) We recommend turning on Play Sea Battle Voice so you can follow commands and raise your chance of winning.
(5) Hide UI lets you better feel the might of the Sea Battle.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_8_2;UnionCommandHelp_8_3

rows.leftIndex:
(1) After the Sea Battle ends, the results screen appears, with detailed battle info in the middle.
(2) The bottom shows this Sea Battle's rewards and penalties.
(3) There are 4 results: Great Victory, Victory, Draw and Defeat.
(4) Great Victory means your side won with more than half of all its warships remaining.
(5) A Draw means the battle lasted 30 minutes and both sides held the same number of outposts.
rows.rightIndex: UnionCommandHelp_9_2;UnionCommandHelp_9_3

rows.leftIndex: (1) Sea Battle also has Support.\nIn Sea Battle, when deploying the 1st and 2nd Fleets, you also need to deploy each fleet's support lineup.\nThe 1st and 2nd Fleets can't share support characters, and their support effects don't affect each other.
rows.rightIndex: (2) Some support effects are affected by warships.\nFor example, Hogback's support effect doesn't work when Blackbeard's Raft is deployed.
